purpose: AFE R1: can the SAM3X ADC's own PGA at gain 4 replace the AFE's +-1.25 V analog stage
firmware: Track B with a debug-only console command =<gain>,<offset>U setting ADC_CGR and ADC_COR on every channel, re-applied by acq_init() after its ADC software reset (which otherwise clears them to gain 1). Not merged; the patch is in 'firmware_patch'.
board_ident: # id: track=B fw=0.2.0 ctlver=4 framever=3 mck=90000000 adcclk=22500000 framebytes=4096 framesamples=2032 uid=442032204e52344d3030363139303038 build=e1ae987+feaf06aa
instrument: the board's own ADC (ets_phase0.py loop, PRBS7, RC 28 DAC / RC 45 ADC, 8 s per run); held-code reads by measure.run_capture at RC 46, 2 s
wiring: DAC0->A0 jumper, scope probe on DAC0 (probes on)

held_code.note: clipped, which shows the gain is applied

reading: Gain 4 applies (swing x3.92) and leaves the eye at the symbol centre fully open at 1.6 Msym/s (0.998, as gain 1). Noise rises x3.3 against a swing x3.9, so relative to the signal it is 15% lower at gain 4. The rise-time figure takes run-level values (57, 60 and 88 ns) at both gains, so it does not separate the PGA's bandwidth from gain 1 and no bandwidth claim is made. The ADC's own noise at gain 4, from the gain-1 and gain-4 readings with the gain-1 floor taken as 0.68 to 0.75 codes (docs/awg.md), is about 0.6 to 1.4 codes: an estimate resting on that assumed floor, not a measurement. A quiet DC source on a spare pin would measure it directly.
